steps.title: Create a new Markdown file for the ADR
steps.instruction: Create a new file named 'ADR-001-example.md' in your project's documentation folder.
steps.hint: You can create this file in any text editor or IDE. The file should have a .md extension to indicate it's a Markdown file.
steps.seedCode: // Create a new file named 'ADR-001-example.md' in your documentation folder
steps.expectedOutcome: A new Markdown file named 'ADR-001-example.md' is created in your documentation folder, ready for ADR content.
successCriteria: File 'ADR-001-example.md' exists in the documentation folder with .md extension.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've created the ADR file. This is the first step in documenting architecture decisions.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've created a file, but make sure it's named exactly 'ADR-001-example.md' and placed in the documentation folder.
steps.feedbackWrong: The file wasn't created correctly. Please create 'ADR-001-example.md' in your documentation folder.

steps.title: Add the ADR header section
steps.instruction: In the 'ADR-001-example.md' file, add a header section with the following Markdown fields: Title, Status, Date, and Decision Makers.
steps.hint: Use Markdown headings and key-value pairs to structure the metadata. Start with a top-level heading for the title.
steps.analogousExample:
# Title

**Status:** Proposed
**Date:** 2023-10-15
**Decision Makers:** Engineering Lead, Product Manager
steps.expectedOutcome: The ADR file now contains a structured header with the required metadata fields.
successCriteria: The header includes Title as a Markdown heading, and Status, Date, and Decision Makers as bolded key-value pairs.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added the standard ADR header with all required metadata fields.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added some header fields, but make sure to include all four: Title, Status, Date, and Decision Makers.
steps.feedbackWrong: The header section is missing or incomplete. Ensure you add Title as a heading and Status, Date, and Decision Makers as bolded key-value pairs.

steps.title: Write the Context section
steps.instruction: Add a Context section below the header that describes the background and problem statement that requires a technical decision.
steps.hint: The Context section should explain what problem you're solving and why a decision is needed.
steps.expectedOutcome: The ADR now includes a Context section that documents the problem background.
successCriteria: The Context section heading and descriptive content are added to the ADR.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added the Context section, which provides essential background for the technical decision.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added the Context heading, but make sure to include descriptive text explaining the problem that requires a decision.
steps.feedbackWrong: The Context section is missing or incomplete. Add a '## Context' heading followed by a description of the problem background.

steps.title: Document the Decision section
steps.instruction: Add a new '## Decision' section header and a paragraph stating the chosen technical approach for the ADR.
steps.hint: Add a Markdown heading '## Decision' followed by a new line and a brief paragraph describing the decision.
steps.expectedOutcome: The ADR document now includes a Decision section with a heading and a description of the chosen approach.
successCriteria: The code contains a '## Decision' heading and a paragraph describing the technical decision.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added the Decision section, clearly documenting the chosen technical approach.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added the heading, but make sure to include a paragraph describing the decision.
steps.feedbackWrong: The Decision section is missing. Add a '## Decision' heading and a paragraph stating the chosen approach.

steps.title: Add the Consequences section
steps.instruction: Add a new '## Consequences' section below the Decision section to document the positive and negative outcomes of this technical decision.
steps.hint: Create a new Markdown heading level 2 with the text 'Consequences', then add bullet points for both positive and negative outcomes.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: Adding a consequences section in a technical document
## Consequences
- Positive: Improved performance
- Negative: Increased maintenance complexity

steps.expectedOutcome: The ADR now includes a Consequences section with placeholders for positive and negative outcomes.
successCriteria: A '## Consequences' heading exists with bullet points for positive and negative outcomes.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added the Consequences section, which helps document the trade-offs of this technical decision.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added the Consequences heading, but make sure to include both positive and negative bullet points.
steps.feedbackWrong: The Consequences section is missing or incomplete. Add a '## Consequences' heading with bullet points for positive and negative outcomes.

steps.title: Create a technical debt tracking table
steps.instruction: Below the Consequences section, add a new section titled 'Technical Debt Tracking' with a Markdown table that has columns for Description, Type, Impact, and Priority.
steps.hint: Create a new heading level 2 (##) for 'Technical Debt Tracking', then add a Markdown table with the specified column headers. You can leave the table rows empty for now.
steps.analogousExample:
## Technical Debt Tracking

| Description | Type | Impact | Priority |
|-------------|------|--------|----------|
|             |      |        |          |

steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added the technical debt tracking table with the required columns. This table will help you systematically document and prioritize technical debt items.

steps.title: Add sample technical debt items
steps.instruction: Add three example technical debt items to the tracking table with realistic descriptions, types, impacts, and priorities.
steps.hint: Fill in the empty rows of the table with concrete examples. For instance, you could add items like 'Unhandled edge cases in user authentication' (type: Code Quality, impact: High, priority: Medium).
steps.analogousExample:
| Legacy payment integration | Integration | High | High |
| Missing unit tests for core modules | Testing | Medium | Low |
| Hardcoded configuration values | Code Quality | Low | Medium |

steps.title: Create an estimation template
steps.instruction: Add an 'Estimation Template' section after the technical debt table with a markdown table containing Task, Complexity, Uncertainty, and Time Estimate columns.
steps.hint: Create a new markdown section header '## Estimation Template' followed by a table with the specified columns. Use pipe syntax for markdown tables.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example markdown table structure
## Section Title
| Column1 | Column2 | Column3 |
|---------|---------|---------|
| Data1   | Data2   | Data3   |
